images.caption: Figure 1:Comparison of representative existing methods and MAGPIE.(a) Existing methods provide semantic or spatial guidance without necessarily exposing an explicit scene for verification. (b) In contrast, MAGPIE instantiates compositional intent as an executable 3D proxy, enabling revision before reference-grounded appearance synthesis.

Figure 2:Overview of MAGPIE.The coding harness converts reference images and an instruction into an executable proxy scene through planning, procedural construction, and geometric and visual refinement. The generator combines the proxy’s structure with reference-specific appearance. MAGPIE-Instruct-3K supports lightweight adaptation to this conditioning.

Figure 3:Overview of MAGPIE-Instruct-3K.Across five compositional tasks, the dataset pairs reference images and instructions with proxy renderings and target images to teach generators to follow the proxy’s structure while preserving reference-specific appearance.
Figure 4:Qualitative comparison of existing models on DreamOmni2 benchmark.

Figure 9:Proxy scenes across refinement budgets.Each row shows the reference images, instruction, and proxies
selected with maximum budgets of 0, 3, and 6 refinement rounds.

Figure 10:Qualitative results on SconeEval.Each row shows the reference images, instruction, selected proxy,
and final image generated with MAGPIE. The examples cover
multi-subject arrangements, articulated poses, and interactions.

Figure 11:Proxy scene comparison across coding agents.Each group shares the same reference images and instruction
and compares the proxy renderings returned by six agents
using the same MAGPIE harness. The examples compare subject inclusion, spatial arrangement,
and the geometric realization of poses and interactions.
